#### 10.3.3 ID.AM-08 Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles {#s-10-3-3}

ID.AM-08.7 The organisation shall prevent unauthorised removal of maintenance equipment containing critical system information of the organisation. ID.AM-08.9 Maintenance tools and portable storage devices shall be inspected as they enter the facility and shall be protected by anti-malware solutions that scan them for malicious code before they are used on the organisation's systems. ID.AM-08.10 The organisation shall verify security controls following maintenance

or repairs/ patching, and take action as appropriate.

#### 10.3.4 PR.DS-02 The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-intransit are protected {#s-10-3-4}

PR.DS-02.1 Portable storage devices containing system data shall be controlled and protected while in transit and in storage.

### 10.4 ANNEX D: LIST OF CONTROLS LINKED TO THE MANAGEMENT ASPECTS FOR THE ASSURANCE LEVEL ‘IMPORTANT’ {#s-10-4}

#### 10.4.1 GV.RM-01 Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders {#s-10-4-1}

GV.RM-01.1 Information/cybersecurity objectives shall be identified, agreed to by organisational stakeholders and approved by senior management

#### 10.4.2 GV.RM-02 Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders {#s-10-4-2}

GV.RM-02.1 Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements shall be defined, documented, approved by senior management, communicated, and maintained.

#### 10.4.3 GV.RM-03 Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes {#s-10-4-3}

GV.RM-03.2 Information and Cybersecurity risks shall be documented, as part of the enterprise risk management processes, formally approved by senior management, and updated when changes occur.

#### 10.4.4 GV.RR-02 Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced. {#s-10-4-4}

GV.RR-02.1 Information security and cyber security roles, responsibilities and authorities for employees, suppliers, customers, and partners shall be documented, reviewed, authorised, kept up-to-date, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally.

#### 10.4.5 ID.RA-05 Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritisation {#s-10-4-5}

ID.RA-05.2 The organisation shall conduct and document risk assessments in which risk is determined by threats, vulnerabilities, impact on business processes and assets, and likelihood of their occurrence.

#### 10.4.6 ID.RA-06 Risk responses are chosen, prioritised, planned, tracked, and communicated. {#s-10-4-6}

ID.RA-06.1 Risk responses shall be identified, prioritised, planned, tracked and communicated.

#### 10.4.7 ID.IM-04 Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved {#s-10-4-7}

ID.IM-04.1 Contingency and continuity plans shall be established, communicated, maintained, tested, validated, and improved.

#### 10.4.8 PR.IR-04 Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained. {#s-10-4-8}

PR.IR-04.1 Adequate resource capacity planning shall ensure that availability of organisation’s critical system information processing, networking, telecommunications, and data storage is maintained.

#### 10.4.9 RC.CO-03 Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders {#s-10-4-9}

RC.CO-03.1 Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities shall be communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders in accordance with established communication procedures.

### 10.5 ANNEX E: LIST OF CONTROLS LINKED TO THE MANAGEMENT ASPECTS FOR THE ASSURANCE LEVEL ‘ESSENTIAL’ {#s-10-5}

#### 10.5.1 GV.RR-02 Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced {#s-10-5-1}

GV.RR-02.2 The organisation shall appoint a senior-level executive information security officer.

#### 10.5.2 GV.SC-01 A cybersecurity supply chain risk management programme, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders. {#s-10-5-2}

GV.SC-01.1 A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes shall be documented, reviewed, updated when changes occur, and approved by organisational stakeholders.

#### 10.5.3 ID.RA-05 Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritisation {#s-10-5-3}

ID.RA-05.3 Risk assessment results shall be disseminated to relevant stakeholders.

#### 10.5.4 ID.IM-03 Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities {#s-10-5-4}

ID.IM-03.9 The organisation shall conduct specialised assessments including indepth monitoring, vulnerability scanning, malicious user testing, insider threat assessment, performance/load testing, and verification and validation testing on the organisation’s critical systems.

#### 10.5.5 ID.IM-04 Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved {#s-10-5-5}

ID.IM-04.2 The organisation shall coordinate the development and testing of Incident Response Plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations with stakeholders to ensure that these plans align with overall organisational goals and enhance resilience.

#### 10.5.6 DE.AE-04 The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood {#s-10-5-6}

DE.AE-04.1 Negative impacts to the organisation’s operations, assets, and individuals resulting from detected events shall be determined and correlated with risk assessment outcomes.
